raw.query: SELECT run_id, window_name, policy, lead_s, sla_metric, p99_ms, n_requests, is_current FROM provenance.v_pool_latency WHERE window_name IN ('burst1','steady24h') AND policy='reactive' AND sla_metric='encoder_delay' ORDER BY window_name, run_id
raw.observed: reactive:reactive_burst1_obs_rho25 encoder_delay p99=1034.827 ms (>1000 ms SLA bound)
raw.claimed: Slow ramps (burst1, calm day) are reactive-scalable at any tested lead (i.e. reactive keeps p99 encoder_delay under 1000 ms at every tested config)
raw.evidence: A current reactive run on burst1 (rho25) breaches the encoder_delay SLA (p99 1034.827 > 1000), so burst1 is not reactive-scalable under all tested reactive configs; lead-sweep subset a2 (L15/30/45/165) and calm-day steady24h do pass.
raw.fix: Qualify the claim to the lead-sweep/config that actually meets SLA (e.g. a2 reactive L≤165, steady24h) or exclude the rho25 reactive controller, since a tested reactive burst1 configuration violates the encoder-delay SLA.
